view: This print turns on one line: whether Amprius reiterates at least $140m for 2026 with a Q3 near or above about $38m, or cuts. The street's FY $133m says it does not believe the guide, so a reiteration with Q3 at $37-39m would be a beat on the line that matters, and roughly 16% short interest plus call-heavy open interest could make that a large up-gap. Against that, the evidence I can see does not show the H2 ramp is in hand. Remaining performance obligations at June 30 were only $36.5m, about 47% of the H2 requirement. Amprius put out no new purchase-order release between August and November, where in the same quarter of 2025 it announced a $35m repeat order. Receivables rose to $40.7m on a $34m quarter (about 109 days of sales). About 31% of Q2 revenue ($10.4m) shipped to Ukraine, where the president warned in late September of a roughly $28bn defence funding gap, a third of it drones. Peers point the other way: Enovix's preliminary Q3 (2026-10-12) beat its guide on drone and defence demand, with early-Q4 orders above all of Q3 revenue, and the $24m European drone order delivers across Q2 2026 to Q1 2027. There is also an automatic shelf (S-3ASR, 2026-10-09), so a raise after the print is possible, though more likely after this window. I end up close to a coin flip with a slight upward lean from the low bar and the positioning, and nothing I would bet on.

recommendation.reason: The decisive question is whether the at-least-$140m guide holds. The public evidence splits: the bar is low (FY consensus $133m under the guide), the drone-battery peer read is strong and positioning is short- and call-heavy, but contracted backlog covered under half of H2, Q3 brought no order announcements, receivables are stretched and Ukraine funding is strained. I cannot show the price is behind in either direction, so there is no mechanism to recommend.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A reiterated or raised FY2026 revenue guide of at least $140m with Q3 revenue at or above about $38m and a Q4 backlog disclosure covering the implied about $40m would make this a clear long. A guide cut toward the $130m area, or an equity raise announced with the release, would make it a short.

self_critique: The case for long is real: management raised the guide only three months ago, with visibility it had then; the company beat revenue consensus in most recent quarters; RPO understates a short-cycle drone business that books and ships inside a quarter; the peer read is strong; and 16% short interest with a call-heavy book could produce a 15-20% gap on a plain reiteration. The case for short is also real: a raise on an S-3ASR into any strength, and the Q1 precedent (-27%) when the release came with dilution. Neither side has a dated piece of evidence showing the price is behind, so 52 stands.
approach_notes: P4 (prove 'priced') helped: the FY consensus below the guide is a concrete measure of the bar rather than an impression. P3's 'freshest data first' was hard to carry out here: the company is quiet between prints and the counterparties (Ukrainian and European drone makers) leave few dated public traces inside a quarter.
